newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle quiet, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Tuesday were quiet, with no sales of slaughter steers or heifers reported, feedlot sources said.
Buyer interest was light, with bids at $66.00 per cwt passed by owners asking $68.00 to mostly $69.00, they said.
Packers were not expected to buy cattle again until Wednesday or Thursday as last week's sales likely supplied adequate inventories for this week, several sources said.
Fed cattle trade, when it does occur, was seen at $68.00, up $1.00 from the bulk of sales late last week, but steady with last Wednesday's top.
Support was expected from smaller numbers of cattle on this week's showlists, compared with last week, and ideas that beef prices will remain firm, the sources said.
However, if beef values dip, the outlook for firm fed cattle prices could dim, they said.
USDA quoted closing beef cut-out values Tuesday up $0.25 per cwt to down $0.11, on 249 loads of fabricated beef sold.
Beef sales were light on Monday but picked up some momentum on Tuesday, but at the uneven prices, sources noted.
